name: HowardHinnant/date
listed_description: Third-party calendar and time zone library for pre-C++20 compilers; the foundation of the C++20 chrono additions.
reason: No reachable numeric comparison against C <ctime> or std::chrono. README.md, the repo tree (ci, cmake, include/date, src, test) and date.h carry no performance claims or benchmarks; the project docs live on howardhinnant.github.io (blocked, not opened). Issue #218 (date::parse seems very slow) has only a hand-written fixed-format parser at about 17 ns with a hot cache, no date::parse timing and no compiler, flags or CPU. WebSearch snippets only, pages unreachable (hosts did not resolve): a 2015 newlib list post reports gmtime_r built on Hinnant's civil_from_days about 13% faster than newlib's gmtime_r on a Cortex-M4 (29.5 s vs 34 s for 3 million conversions), and a Dec 2025 LLVM libc patch reports 14.4 ns vs 17.4 ns for a Joffe plus Hinnant civil_from_days conversion; both test the published algorithm in other codebases, not this library. Maintained: latest commit shown 2026-10-22, MIT licence.

name: immer
listed_description: Library of persistent immutable collections for C++ that avoids heavy copying by sharing structure between versions.
reason: Directional claim, no reachable numbers. README says benchmark results are collected from CI at public.sinusoid.es (host did not resolve); the repo holds benchmark code only (benchmark/vector/paper/push.cpp registers nonius runs of immer flex_vector against librrb, std::vector (transient only), std::list and chunkedseq) and no committed results; docs/*.rst have no timings. Issue #28 has the maintainer saying std::vector is somewhat better at small sizes and flex_vector much faster for concatenating thousands of elements (O(log(n+m)) vs O(n+m)), with no figures. The numbers are in the ICFP 2017 paper Persistence for the Masses, whose hosts (Scribd, EPFL infoscience) did not resolve; search snippets give only its abstract (performance comparable to mutable arrays in many situations). Maintained: latest commit shown 2026-02-25, BSL-1.0, 2.9k stars.
